newsitem.title: India: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and
political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by
Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi
biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch
for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
UNITED FRONT WANTS BIHAR CHIEF MINISTER TO QUIT

The Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) decision to charge Bihar chief minister and Janata Dal (JD) chief Laloo Prasad Yadav in the animal husbandry scam could not have come at a worse moment for the barely week-old I.K. Gujral government. The overwhelming feeling in the ruling United Front (UF) was that Yadav should step down as chief minister in the interest of the UF's credibility. So far, only the Left parties have publicly asked him to quit.
Indian Express
DEFIANT LALOO RULES OUT RESIGNATION

Laloo Prasad Yadav ruled out resigning from office, after the announcement that he was one of the 56 to be charged in the 9.5 billion rupee animal husbandary scare. He claimed there was a conspiracy behind the hasty decision. Meanwhile, the prime minister refused to comment on the demand of the four Left parties for Laloo Yadav's resignation. Laloo was said to be toying with the idea of floating a regional party to fight his case.
The Economic Times
ICICI TO REFUND 70 PCT OF AMOUNT MOPPED UP BY BOND ISSUE

Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) decided to refund around 70 percent of the 25 billion rupees mopped up through its 7.5 billion rupees bond issue. The bond issue, which closed for subscription, had been a hit with its 16.25 percent yield in a falling interest rate scenario.
PER CAPITA WEALTH AT $25,000: WORLD BANK

India's per capita national wealth is $25,000 and savings represents only 8 per cent of her wealth, according to a new method of calculation suggested by the World Bank's environment department. The new figures, which contrasts with the $340 per capita income, are a result of the new method. A document explaining the new method has been circulated by the World Bank to member states and academia for approval.
17.95 BLN RUPEE FOREIGN INVESTMENT PROPOSALS APPROVED

The government approved 17.95 billion rupees' worth of foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals. The proposals included three airline projects, ABB's 100 percent investment company involving two billion rupees and GEC-Alsthom's railway equipment project. CS First Boston's proposal to set up a broking company with an investment of 175 million rupees was cleared, along with James Capel's application to hike its stake in the Indian venture. Bharati Telecom's proposal to set up of an investment company with foreign investment of 4.38 billion rupees was also cleared along with Germany's Eurokapital Aktiengesellschaft's proposal for a multi-fuel based power plant.
Financial Express
INTERNATIONAL PRICE FOR OUTPUT IN OFFING

The Petroleum Ministry planned to kick start production in marginal oil fields in possession of state owned drilling companies by providing international prices for their output. The ministry asked for a list of marginal fields which were unviable in terms of internal rate of return when computed on oil prices offered by the government, but became attractive when returns were calculated on the basis of import parity price. Sources said the ministry had offered to take up some of these fields on a case by case basis for provision of international prices.
BROADCASTING BILL MAY ALLOW 100 PCT CROSS MEDIA OWNERSHIP

The government would allow 100 percent cross media ownership in local terrestrial broadcasting companies in the proposed Broadcasting Bill. The proposed 20 percent cap in case of cross media ownership would now be applicable to national level broadcasting companies and satellite broadcasters. Government sources said the Information and Broadcasting Ministry had moved a cabinet note on this issue.
Business Standard
LG ELECTRONICS PLANS $300 MLN INVESTMENTS IN INDIA

LG Electronics of South Korea has identified India as one of the four global production bases for colour televisions (CTVs) and components, apart from China, Indonesia and Brazil. LG earmarked 15 percent of its total global investments and planned to invest about $300 million in its Indian business. The Korean consumer electronics giant has targeted a 14 percent share of an estimated 12 million piece CTVs market in India by 2005. LG also decided to expand the capacity of its picture tubes unit in Madhya Pradesh from 750,000 at present to three million pieces over the next few years.
AIR INDIA PLANS 10 BLN RUPEE ISSUE TO FUND PURCHASE

Air India proposed to float a 10 billion rupee public issue to fund the purchase of medium capacity long range aircraft within three years. The timing of the issue would depend on market conditions. The move was based on recommendations of ICICI Securities which was requisitioned by the national flag carrier to draft a financial restructuring programme. The issue would widen Air India's current equity base of 1.54 billion rupees.
The Observer
CENTRAL BANK SETS UP PANEL ON MONEY MARKET

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced the setting up of a standing committee to look into the money market, indicating its seriousness about developing the secondary market into a vibrant liquid market. RBI said the terms of reference of the committee would include strengthening the role of the call money market in the financial system and recommend measures relating to the participants, instruments and the institutional arrangements for development of the call money market. The committee would function in a manner similar to the committees on foreign exchange market and the government securities market.
POWER MAY BE PRIVATISED IN RAJASTHAN

Electricity distribution would be fully privatised in Rajasthan in a phased manner by 2002, according to the Electricity Distribution Privatisation Strategy Document. The state government planned to adopt a four-stage privatisation strategy. The first stage would cover the areas in which distribution losses were high and where private contractors could increase revnue collection.
Business Line
NEW AIR PACT WITH CHINA LIKELY

India planned to sign a fresh air services agreement (ASA) with China, paving the way for establishing air links between the two countries for the first time. The bilateral talks on civil aviation would be headed by the Civil Aviation Secretary who would hold talks with the Civil Aviation Administration of China. India's last ASA with China expired in December 1988. Since then, there were various aborted attempts to revive talks between the two.
